source.author: verg
source.text: Non prius aspicies, ubi fessum aetate parentem liqueris Anchisen; superet coniunxne Creüsa, Ascaniusque puer?
source.text_original: Non prius aspicies, ubi fessum aetate parentem / liqueris Anchisen; superet coniunxne Creüsa, / Ascaniusque puer?
source.text_english: Will you not look first to where you left your father Anchises, worn out by age; whether your wife Creusa survives, and your young Ascanius?

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: donat et Iphiclo pelagus iuvenumque labores Aesonides, fessum Phylace quem miserat aevo non iam operum in partem, monitus sed tradat ut acres magnorumque viros qui laudibus urat avorum.
reuse.text_original: donat et Iphiclo pelagus iuvenumque labores / Aesonides, fessum Phylace quem miserat aevo / non iam operum in partem, monitus sed tradat ut acres / magnorumque viros qui laudibus urat avorum.
reuse.text_english: And the son of Aeson also grants to Iphiclus the sea and the labors of the youths, whom Phylace had sent forth, now weary with age, not now for a share in the tasks, but that he might hand him over, as instructed, to sharp, great men who would kindle him with the praises of his ancestors.
